newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSTANT VIEW - Australian June trade data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Australian June trade data.

text.p: Australia posted a trade surplus of A$$1.964 billion in June, up from the A$787 million surplus recorded in May, the Australian Bureau of Statistics reported.
Exports of goods and services rose 20 percent in June while imports of goods and services rose eight percent.
The surplus, a record, was boosted by A$1.8 billion by the inclusion of proceeds from the sale of gold reserves by the Reserve Bank of Australia.
A selection of economists' immediate reactions follows.
JOHN PETERS, SENIOR ECONOMIST, WESTPAC BANK:

"Pretty much on expectations with the inclusion of that A$1.8 billion in gold. Imports up, we were expecting a rise there, but really in terms of the market, markets weren't really focusing on it, they're still waiting for the rate cut. No market impact or policy implications from that number."
CRAIG JAMES, SENIOR ECONOMIST, COLONIAL STATE BANK:

"Taking out the gold sales, the surplus was a little bit higher than expected. However, we will have to watch trends in imports of goods in future months as there appears to be a modest uptick occurring. If we start to see a recovery occurring then rate cut expectations go off the wire and we start to talk about when is the first time they are going to tighten, I suppose, ... but it is early days yet."
STEPHEN KOUKOULAS, CHIEF ECONOMIST, CITIBANK AUSTRALIA:

"We are still running a reasonable position on our goods and services account. The services area is still in surplus and is an indication that the economy is still happening, and the export sector, even excluding the gold, is still holding up reasonably well. The trade account is not too bad and should be mildly supportive to the markets."
TONY MEER, ECONOMIST, DEUTSCHE MORGAN GRENFELL:

"Even taking out the fact you have got the gold sales in there, obviously we have had a reasonably positive trend in the goods and services now for some time. And that does reflect on the one hand the slowdown in the economy but also it is a function of the very positive trend in the services balance. I think that is something really which hasn't had a lot of focus on it."
STEPHEN ROBERTS, CHIEF ECONOMIST, UBS AUSTRALIA:

"By the time you take out the significant one-offs, the underlying position of exports of goods and services was in surplus, but a surplus that declined a little running in June compared with May. You are still going to get a healthy contribution from net exports of goods and services in second quarter GDP, but part of that will be offset by the stock adjustment for the Reserve Bank gold sales."
